# Attempt 3: the summary now carries the evidence criterion 1 used to assert

RED is record 32 and GREEN is record 33. The RED's words were plain: `KeyError: 'slices'` four times
and `KeyError: 'spending'` once, from `pytest harness/tests/test_loop.py -k RunEvidence`. The sixth
test in the class, that the summary writes nothing, passed before and after: it is what criteria 2 and
7 rest on and it was not supposed to move.

What the summary reported before, on this ticket's own journal: the attempt, the authorisation, the
criteria, the defects, what is met and unmet, the question batches, the stage, the stops and the ticket
file. Nothing about who worked a slice, on what, or what it cost. The three facts the amended criterion
1 names were true only as prose in a note, which is the weakest kind of evidence this harness accepts
and the kind criterion 7 exists to forbid.

What it reports now, per slice, read from the journal and from nothing else: whether the slice was
delegated and to which agent, from the `--agent` declaration on the two checks the tdd record cites;
the `--model` declaration beside what the route decided, so a slice that ran on something other than
its route is visible rather than asserted; and the session's own output tokens with the subagents'
reported apart from them, by calling `harness budget` rather than reading the logs a second time.

On SEEN-112's own journal it says slice 1 (2 points, cited by record 19, checks 10 and 11) was
delegated to `seen-implementer` on opus as routed, and slice 2 (1 point, checks 14 and 15) the same.
The spending line says this session at 199,252 output tokens and 117 tool calls against a 60,000
budget, with 228,610 across five subagents reported apart from it. That figure is the ticket's own
argument, on its own record: hand orchestration is what costs, and it is over by more than three times.

One reading subtlety worth keeping in the record, because it is the kind that is wrong silently:
`citations()` reads every tdd advance since the plan was accepted and takes the latest citation per
position, rather than the latest record. A rework round cites `position: null`, so a reader that took
only the last tdd record would leave a reworked ticket's slices with no checks at all, and a reader
that counted greens would shift every slice after one that recorded two. This ticket, with three
attempts and a null-position round in the middle of them, is exactly the journal that would have
exposed neither until someone read a wrong answer.

Two things named and left. `delegated` is null before a tdd record cites a slice's checks, so a session
asking for the summary mid-tdd sees nothing about the slice it has just proved: the citation is the only
place a check is bound to a slice by number, and a second reader that counted greens would be a second
answer to a question that already has one. And `RunEvidenceTest` pins `[routing] shadow` true in its
own project copy of the thresholds, because the off-route slice it builds is one the tdd gate would
refuse with shadow off; when SEEN-109's window flips the real flag, that fixture is the thing to
revisit, because `as_routed: false` becomes a gate refusal rather than a summary line.
